title: Traffic handshake + stress-run scoping kickoff
next_steps: Redwood to share benchmark template and example harness adapter (by 2027-03-23)
Customer to provide 2 representative client scripts and 1 traffic profile (by 2027-03-25)
Security: customer to review SOC2/ISO packet and confirm additional controls needed (by 2027-03-26)
action_items: Omar (Redwood) - prepare KV-cache warm start checklist and stream vs batch test plan - 2027-03-24
Samir (BlueCrest) - share two production client scripts + traffic histogram - 2027-03-25
summary: Kickoff for a POC stress-run and harness integration to validate throughput and tail-latency SLOs.

Primary success criteria: 95th percentile latency < 400ms for streaming, sustained throughput of 250 qps non-streaming with 99% availability during test window, and reproducible harness integration with customer scripts.
Decision points: streaming vs non-streaming default for pilot, KV cache warmup strategy, and timeline for lab runs and pilot.
topics: KV cache warmup and cold start strategy
transcript: [00:00] Jana (Redwood AE): hey good afternoon everyone thanks for joining i know we had a busy week so we'll try to keep the kickoff tight. i'm jana, i'll run the agenda.
[00:18] Marta (BlueCrest): hi jana, thanks. i'm marta. excited to get this moving, we've been wanting to validate production cost and tail more precisely before we commit the dedicated pool.
[00:32] Omar (Redwood SE): quick intro from me — omar, infra and benchmarking — i'll own the harness adapter work. we'll need two sample client flows and the traffic histogram you mentioned.

[00:45] Samir (BlueCrest): yes, we have two main flows: a short chat completion (avg 32 tokens) and a long form summarization pipeline (avg 1.2k tokens). i'll share scripts, one is in python, one is in node. both call through our edge proxy.

[01:10] Priya (Redwood): the core goals we've heard — verify throughput per GPU, tail latencies, and warmup behavior for KV cache. putting exact numbers on the call will help, marta if you can confirm your SLOs?

[01:28] Marta (BlueCrest): sure, our product SLO is 95th < 400ms for interactive chat. For batch summarization we care more about throughput and 99th shouldn't exceed 2.5s. cost target is under $0.02 per 1k tokens processed, rough number.
[01:55] Connor (Redwood Product): want to flag that cost target will depend heavily on quantization and batching configs; we'll recommend a profile but we need telemetry to validate the $ numbers.

[02:10] Nina (BlueCrest, Security): and on security, we'll need KMS integration and proof of no persistent customer PII leaving our VPC. SOC2 packet is in review but we may ask for additional audit hooks.
[02:28] Jana (Redwood): understood. action items later. ok moving to workload sizing — samir, can you walk through the traffic hist we asked for?

[02:40] Samir (BlueCrest): right so typical qps now is low, like 20 qps peak, but for launch we want to test up to 250 qps non-streaming and 120 concurrent streaming sessions. the distributions are bursty, we have diurnal spikes and sudden ramp (flash sales) — sent the CSV earlier but i'll reattach.

[03:10] Omar (Redwood): perfect. for the harness we support two modes: streaming mode where the client keeps the connection open and we push tokens incrementally, and non-streaming (batch) where requests complete once full response emitted. each has different batching behavior and tail characteristics.
[03:32] Marta (BlueCrest): our chat uses streaming in prod today. the summarizer is non-streaming. i'd like both covered in the POC.

[03:45] Priya (Redwood): noted. important tradeoff: streaming gives lower time-to-first-token and perceived latency but can hurt throughput if we can't efficently multiplex. we should plan mixed-mode runs.
[04:05] Samir (BlueCrest): what do you mean by multiplex? our edge does connection reuse but not client-side batching, currently single request per connection.

[04:20] Omar (Redwood): i mean the server can accept many streaming sessions and interleave GPU work; it relies on small attention kernels and KV cache reuse. A misconfigured mux will result in lower GPU utilization for streaming, raising cost.
[04:45] [crosstalk] Evan (SRE): sorry interrupt — what about cold-starts? our Summarizer sees big cold tail due to KV cache not warmed between requests.

[04:55] Omar (Redwood): good point — we'll include KV-cache warm start experiments: 1) full warmup ramp (send representative prefixes), 2) periodic keepalive, 3) cold-only to measure worst-case tail. each run will have warmup windows and measurement windows.

[05:20] Jana (Redwood): timeline proposal: send template + adapter example in 48h, customer provides scripts and hist in 72h, run lab stress-runs next week (3 day window), then review results and decide pilot. does that work?
[05:40] Marta (BlueCrest): yes that's fine. one ask: can you reproduce traffic from behind our edge proxy (we don't want to change client auth flows)?
[05:55] Omar (Redwood): yes, we can run the harness in proxy-passive mode — the adapter will replay real client flows including auth headers. we'll need a sandbox token and sanitized logs.
[06:10] Nina (BlueCrest): we can't share production tokens; we'll provide a staging CA and ephemeral creds. also need to confirm retention settings — no logs containing PII persist beyond 7 days.
[06:28] Priya (Redwood): we support per-run retention TTL and can redact bodies before storage. we'll note that in the security doc.
[06:40] [10s pause/noise]

[06:50] Omar (Redwood): on metrics — please baseline what you currently measure (p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, tokens/sec). the harness will emit per-request traces and an aggregated CSV for comparison.
[07:10] Samir (BlueCrest): we have p50/p95/p99 at edge but not per-model tokens/sec, that's on our wishlist. can you instrument that?
[07:22] Connor (Redwood): yes we'll produce a telemetry sheet mapping request IDs to model, variant, and kernel profile. shared link: drive/bluecrest/benchmark-harness (will upload).

[07:40] Marta (BlueCrest): another thing — fallback behavior. if your primary model hits capacity do you have automatic fallthrough to a cheaper quantized variant? we want to test correctness under that scenario.

[07:55] Omar (Redwood): absolutely, we'll include a model-variant failover test. the harness will simulate load that triggers fallback policies; we'll capture correctness deltas and token-cost impact.
[08:10] Priya (Redwood): slight caveat: for streaming the client may see partial tokens during fallback; we'll explain user-visible behaviors in the test report.
[08:25] Samir (BlueCrest): perfect. about acceptance gates — can we list them now? i'd like clarity what passes the POC.

[08:35] Jana (Redwood): yes, draft acceptance gates: (1) end-to-end harness runs reproduce customer traffic with <5% script-error rate; (2) streaming 95th < 400ms for chat across measurement window; (3) non-streaming sustained 250 qps with 99% success and 99th < 2.5s; (4) KV cache warmup reduces p99 by >30% vs cold; (5) telemetry artifacts and adapter code delivered.
[09:10] Marta (BlueCrest): that looks reasonable. can we add an SLA target for availability during the test? say 99% test availability?
[09:22] Connor (Redwood): we can commit to 99% platform availability for the scheduled lab window; we'll also note expected variability from the customer's network path.
[09:35] Evan (SRE): how will you simulate client-side retries? our production has a 2-retry logic that amplifies load during bursts.
[09:45] Omar (Redwood): include retry semantics in the adapter — we can replay with your retry policy. we should also set a max QPS envelope to avoid blowing up upstream dependencies in the lab.
[10:00] Nina (BlueCrest): security question: will the harness ever write full request/response bodies to Redwood logs? we need confirmation on redaction and KMS at rest.

[10:12] Priya (Redwood): default is to redact request bodies; for debugging we can enable full capture with customer's explicit permission and short TTL. everything at rest encrypted with customer KMS on Private deployment; hosted kept encrypted with our KMS unless using Redwood Private.
[10:32] Marta (BlueCrest): ok note, we prefer Private or dedicated with customer-managed keys for the pilot. we'll clarify in the security doc.
[10:45] Jana (Redwood): good. practical items for the harness adapter — omar: what files do you need from bluecrest?

[10:52] Omar (Redwood): sample client scripts (2), traffic histogram CSV, staging auth method + ephemeral creds, list of model variants and tokenization specifics if custom, and a short network diagram. prefer github repo or zip.

[11:10] Samir (BlueCrest): i'll bundle those. note the summarizer uses streaming for chunking internally but final response is non-streamed; the node script does some proto-level buffering which may affect perceived latency.
[11:30] Priya (Redwood): we'll make the adapter deterministic and add a shim for the buffering so we can toggle immediate flush vs buffered behavior in test runs.
[11:45] Marta (BlueCrest): are you planning to run the harness from your cloud or can we host the runner in our account to reduce network variance?

[11:55] Omar (Redwood): both options possible. for initial lab runs we'll run in our lab to speed iteration; if you want a more realistic run we can deploy the runner into your VPC (Redwood Private) and run there — that'll be next phase.

[12:10] Jana (Redwood): timeline check: if we get artifacts by Thursday we can run initial stress tests next Monday-Thursday, deliver results on Friday. Pilot (in-customer VPC) would be mid-April if everything looks good. any blockers?
[12:26] Marta (BlueCrest): concern on data residency for logs if hosted — we'll check with legal but likely want the pilot in VPC. not a blocker for the lab.
[12:40] Connor (Redwood): we'll annotate the report with what was run in hosted vs private and include guidance on moving to dedicated pools.
[12:52] Samir (BlueCrest): small ask — can you include cost-projection calculations per 1M tokens under the different configurations (quantized vs fp16) in the final report?
[13:05] Omar (Redwood): yes we'll produce cost buckets: token-cost at steady state, cost delta for fallbacks, and amortized cost of KV warmup strategies.
[13:20] [noise/brief pause]

[13:30] Jana (Redwood): ok to recap next steps — i'll send the benchmark template and the adapter example; omar will publish the KV warm-start checklist; samir will share scripts and histogram; nina will confirm security constraints. we'll reconvene after the lab run with results and a pass/fail sheet. any final questions?
[13:50] Marta (BlueCrest): no further questions, thanks everyone. excited to see the warmup results.
[14:00] Jana (Redwood): thanks all, meeting end. (recording stopped)
